- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion bias.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently over-optimistically forecasts higher peaks; cap forecast at 1.2x recent high or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 3-period moving average or add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid over-leverage.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price at end of period; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to anticipate correction; add 1–2% downward bias in next 5–7 days if sentiment <0.30.
- Avoid forecasting below 50% of recent 18-day low unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.10) — model tends to underpredict bottoming in bear markets.
